title: Make the sign-up form accessible
ticketBrief:
# Ticket FE-101
QA reports that screen-reader users cannot tell what the two sign-up fields are for: the form uses placeholders instead of labels, and the inputs have the wrong types.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Each field has a visible `<label>` linked with `for`/`id`.
- The email field uses `type="email"`; the password field uses `type="password"`.
- The button is explicitly `type="submit"`.

steps.title: Fix the form
steps.instruction: Edit index.html so the form meets the acceptance criteria.

checks.label: Email field has a linked label
Password field has a linked label
Fields use the right input types

hints.body: A label is linked to an input when its for attribute equals the input's id.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Sign up</title></head>
<body>
  <form action="/signup" method="post">
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>
    <label for="password">Password</label>
    <input id="password" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" required>
    <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Sign up</title></head>
<body>
  <form action="/signup" method="post">
    <input type="text" placeholder="Email">
    <input type="text" placeholder="Password">
    <button>Sign up</button>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

title: Give the shop page a semantic structure
ticketBrief:
# Ticket FE-102
The landing page is built entirely from `<div>`s, which makes it hard for assistive technology and search engines to understand.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Use `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<footer>` landmarks.
- The page title "Welcome" is the page's `<h1>`.
- Remove the old generic wrappers (`class="header"`, `id="content"`, `class="footer"`).

steps.title: Restructure the page
steps.instruction: Edit index.html to meet the acceptance criteria.

checks.label: Page uses header, nav, main and footer

title: Build a product card (practice, checked in your browser)
ticketBrief:
# Ticket FE-103
Build a product card inside the page.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A `.card` container.
- An image with an `alt` attribute.
- A heading (`h2`) with the product name.
- An *Add to cart* button.

_These checks run in your browser, so a pass counts as completed practice but earns no ELO or skill evidence._

steps.title: Build the card
steps.instruction: Edit index.html; the preview shows your card and the checks update live.

checks.label: The card image has alt text
The card has an h2 heading
The card has an Add to cart button
